newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-ROCKETS SPEED BY SUPERSONICS TO END SEATTLE JINX.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-ROCKETS SPEED BY SUPERSONICS TO END SEATTLE JINX.

text.p: Charles Barkley had 26 points and 15 rebounds and Clyde Drexler added 23 points as the Houston Rockets snapped a 13-game losing streak against the Seattle SuperSonics Saturday with a 109-100 road victory.
The Rockets (20-2) improved to 10-1 on the road this season. Hakeem Olajuwon had nine points and 10 rebounds for Houston, which had not won in Seattle since April 17, 1993.
"We played very well," said Barkley. "We've got a very good team and this was a very big step for us. They're the best team in the West until somebody beats them."

Said Drexler: "We wanted to establish ourselves early and we were able to do that by hitting the open threes. We knew Seattle was going to double (team) the big fellow (Olajuwon), so we were able to shoot the ball."
Shawn Kemp had 28 points and 10 rebounds and Gary Payton added 16 points and five assists for the SuperSonics (16-9), last year's NBA Championship runners-up.

In Chicago, Michael Jordan scored 29 points and Dennis Rodman returned from a two-game suspension to grab a season-high 23 rebounds as the Chicago Bulls edged the Charlotte Hornets 87-82 for their third straight win.

Jordan was not an offensive factor down the stretch but made a key block on a practically unstoppable Matt Geiger in the final minute. Geiger scored 18 of his 20 points in the fourth period, including 16 straight Charlotte points.
"We were lucky to win tonight," Jordan said. "Geiger almost took the game away from us at the end."

Rodman was suspended two games by the Bulls for a profane tirade against referees on Sunday. The Bulls beat Minnesota and New Jersey in his absence. "It was great having Dennis back in the game tonight," Jordan said. "His intensity was good and he did a nice job on (Anthony) Mason."
A pair of three-pointers by Toni Kukoc helped the Bulls down the stretch as Chicago improved to 20-3.
Glen Rice scored 25 points for the Hornets.

In San Antonio, David Robinson shook off back spasms to score 27 points, including the game-winning layup with 8.5 seconds left, as the San Antonio Spurs claimed a 106-105 victory over the Dallas Mavericks.
Robinson, who had 10 rebounds, left with back spasms in the second quarter, but returned prior to the end of the half.
"That was huge for us tonight, to get this one," Robinson said. "Now we feel like this is the start of something."
George McCloud scored 28 points on 9-of-14 shooting for Dallas, but missed a potential game-winner at the buzzer.

The win was the first for the Spurs with Robinson in the lineup and only their fourth in 21 games overall this season. Robinson, who missed the first 18 games with a lower back strain, was 10-of-13 from the field in 25 minutes.
In Miami, Alonzo Mourning recorded 26 points, 10 rebounds and five blocked shots and the Miami Heat survived a late rally by the Toronto Raptors to post their 13th win in their last 14 games, 89-88.
Sasha Danilovic scored 15 points while Hardaway added 15 and six assists for Miami. Walt Williams totalled 18 points, six rebounds and six steals for Toronto.
In Atlanta, Mookie Blaylock and Christian Laettner scored 17 points apiece to lead a balanced attack as the Hawks won their eighth straight home game, 106-81 over the slumping Philadelphia 76ers.
Derrick Coleman had 21 points and 10 boards for the 76ers.
In New York, Chris Childs had 20 points and nine assists and Patrick Ewing had 18 points and 11 rebounds as the Knicks handed the Denver Nuggets their 10th straight loss 89-82.
Antonio McDyess scored 29 points and LaPhonso Ellis added 23 as the Nuggets lost for the 14th time in 15 games.
The Knicks extended their winning streak to six games.
At Minnesota, Terrell Brandon scored 12 of his 22 points in the fourth quarter when the Cleveland Cavaliers rallied to beat the Timberwolves for the 10th time in 11 games, 101-93.
The Cavs had 37 points in the final period, a total that matched or bettered 11 of Cleveland's one-half totals.
Tom Gugliotta scored 21 points for Minnesota.
In Milwaukee, Vin Baker had 27 points and 17 rebounds and Glenn Robinson added 27 points to lead the Milwaukee Bucks to a 101-91 victory over the New Jersey Nets.
Robinson also had seven rebounds and eight assists for the Bucks. Robert Pack led the Nets with 23 points.
At Utah, John Stockton and Greg Ostertag scored 16 points apiece and the Utah Jazz used big bursts in each of the last three quarters to trounce the ailing Orlando Magic 101-68.
Howard Eisley scored 14 points and Karl Malone added 11 for the Jazz, who have won 16 of 17 games. Rony Seikaly scored 23 points for the Magic, losers of six of their last seven.

At Los Angeles, Darrick Martin made 15-of-15 free throws, including six in the final 2:34, and the Los Angeles Clippers gave coach Bill Fitch his 900th career victory in a 106-94 victory over the Sacramento Kings.
Terry Dehere scored 16 points for the Clippers. Martin, 0-8 from the field, scored all his points from the foul line.
Fitch became the fourth coach to reach 900 wins joining Lenny Wilkens, Red Auerbach and Dick Motta.
Mitch Richmond scored 33 points for the Kings.
